utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, The Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. I'd just like to put on the record that the Chamber was informed about an exchange of e-mails about the timing of the submissions the Chamber asked for. I do understand that the Gotovina Defence has filed a submission and sent a curtsy copy to the Prosecution, and it seems that this has resolved the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, I'm not entirely sure it resolved the matter, Your Honour, in the sense that Prosecution's last e-mail indicated the nature of the problem. We're doing our best to conform to the schedule. I believe we will do so. I would urge as a somewhat separate matter that where possible and I, appreciate the fact that there are circumstances where the exigencies of time may dictate otherwise, that we try not to impose orders that absolutely require people to come in on weekends to do that work. I know there's an understanding which unfortunately is true, that everyone works weekends any way but to actually schedule matters to be done on a Sunday, I think, is a matter that should be avoided, where possible. In any event, we're -- we believe we will be able to file a response by the noon deadline. We'll advise the Court if the matter is otherwise. At the moment, I think we're on schedule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's understood and appreciated that the parties would say like to avoid, to the extent possible, any forced labour during the weekend. That's on the record. And -- yes. Is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No protective measures, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then Mr. Lausic would be your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Lausic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you give evidence in this Court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require that you make a solemn declaration, that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. May I invite to you make that solemn declaration, of which the text is now handed out to you by Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lausic. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lausic, you will first be examined by Mr. Tieger. Mr. Tieger is counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Tieger, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Lausic.

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Lausic, let me begin with a pure formality. Can you state your full name for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC
utterances.text: My name is Mate Lausic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Lausic, I wanted to move on to some of the formalities of utilizing some of the materials you've provided previously, so let me ask you these questions. In 2004, on the 13th and 14th of May, is it correct that you were interviewed by representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor, and, at that time, your rights under Rule 42 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence were read and the interview was tape-recorded. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And subsequently, on the 11th of August, is it correct that the interview of the 13th and 14th was reduced to statement form and that you had an opportunity to review the accuracy of that statement and initial the pages of that statement and sign it at that time?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC
utterances.text: It is it correct that in the month of August of 2004, the transcript in the English language was read back to me; that was my statement in the capacity of a suspect that -- that was a statement taken of me in May of 2004. And over a couple of days in the month of August, the OTP investigators, with the assistance of interpreters, went through that May 2004 transcript with me, and I signed a witness statement in the English language back in 2004. At that time it was read back to me, there was no audio or videotape given to me. But up until the 17th of December, 2008, I had not been able to see either the transcript of the interview of me as a suspect of May 2004, or the statement that I gave in August of 2004 in the Croatian language, the language that I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's take it a step at a time then.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I could ask that 65 ter 7032 be called up.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Lausic, do you recognise 65 ter 7032 now on the screen as the statement you referred to a moment ago, that was read back to you and that you signed in August of 2004?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now you may have foreshadowed the next question, but I will ask you that. Did that statement, the August 2004 statement, accurately reflect the information you provided the representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor in August of 2004?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC
utterances.text: I said that I saw that statement in the Croatian language for the first time on the 17th of December, 2008, when investigator Brian Foster handed me the Croatian version in the Zagreb office of the ICTY. As I went through the Croatian version of my witness statement of August 2004, I observed some errors that were of purely technical nature and others that were quite substantial in nature. If I may indicate one difference between the English and Croatian versions, on the first page, is that of rank. In the Croatian version, it is said that I'm a retired Croatian army Colonel General, whereas in the Croatian general it says that I was a Major-General. Have I noted a substantial number of such errors in the notebook that I have taken along with me here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Lausic, it is my intention to provide the Chamber with this statement in its most accurate form and, of course, I intend, therefore, to ask you if you had any corrections to make to the transcript, having reviewed it, so perhaps it's best if we -- if you advise the Chamber of any inaccuracies in the statement that you noted and that you indicate those by paragraph number so the Chamber can follow in the transcript it has -- in the copy of the statement it has before it where those corrections should be made.

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that, and I would kindly ask to be given that possibility, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. So the first correction you indicated, Mr. Lausic, with respect to your rank at retirement is found at what paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC
utterances.text: That's page 1, the one I can see on the screen before me, where it says current -- or rather former occupation. In the English version it says Croatian army Colonel General; whereas, in the English version, it says the Croatian army Major-General. That's the difference. So the correct version is Major-General -- or Colonel General depending on ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I'm not sure if we have a translation dilemma because I have heard both versions for the cover page reference, both to Colonel General and Major-General. And I'm not sure it's helpful if I repeat to the witness that the English says Colonel General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the English version says Colonel General, and that's -- is that correct, or is it Major-General? Should it be Major-General?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct. I am the retired Croatian army Colonel General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what the English version says.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that seems to be correct then. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Lausic, if you could move through the statement and identify any other corrections you wish to be made.

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, please. On page 2, paragraph 3. Paragraph 3, line 4, the Croatian translation of the English original states that on the 1st of February, 1971, I was admitted into the state Security Service in the city of Zagreb, which is incorrect. It is it correct that on that date, the 1st of February, 1971, I was admitted into the public security service of the city of Zagreb, and the difference is a crucial one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll read the English to you. "On the 1st of February, 1971, I was accepted to the secretariat of public security of the city of Zagreb, which was the name of the police in Zagreb at that time." Is that correct, or is that not correct? Because it reads in English the public security.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the next one, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Also on page 2, in paragraph 3, the text goes on to state that in September or October of 1971, I passed a professional exam and became the authorised staff member, whereas I became the authorised official of the public security service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "Staff member" is then corrected into official of the public security service.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's on the record. Please proceed, next one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 3, paragraph 10, line 2, the 6th Department was charged with the security of protected persons and structures. The term "structure" is incorrect here. What was referred to was protected persons and buildings or facilities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's on the record. The next one, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Also on page 3, in paragraph 10, line 8: "Since I became head of security of the President of the republic." The term in the B/C/S "nacelnik," head or chief is incorrect. My correct term in Croatian was "sef." Again, head or chief in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It now then would read: "By becoming the sef of the security for the President of the republic." That's on the record.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next one, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 4, paragraph 14, line 1. "On the 1st of December, 1991, I took over the command of the military police administration upon an oral order." Instead of the word, "I took over the command," what should be stated is, I took over the position of the chief of the military police administration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's on the record. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 5, paragraph 15, line 4, the criteria that the Brigade commanders had to apply when selecting military policemen is being referred to, and the translation says: "There were no criteria for the selection of men, so that only the physical characteristics of men were taken into consideration, and therefore the men had to be physically strong, two metres tall, 100 kilograms in weight in order to discipline a soldier, et cetera et cetera." This is incorrect. This was merely a rhetorical figure that I presented. These were not the actual criteria the commanders applied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would it be correct to understand it that the criteria were that they should be tall and strong people, without any numbers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's on the record. Then physically strong, tall and strong people, without any reference to specific length or specific weight. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 6, the continuation of paragraph 18 from page 5. Line 3: "But professionally speaking or on the professional level, they became part of a company." Instead of the words "professional level," what should be stated is "establishment-wise."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We are in the English on the fourth line from the bottom, page 5. They remained with that Brigade, but establishment-wise they became a part of the company, and the company was within a battalion." That's on the record. Please, could you give us the next correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Further down the page, continuation of paragraph 18 from page 5, line 4: "That platoon had to submit reports to the company commander." Instead of -- well, in the B/C/S prijavak, the term "izvjestaj" should be used.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter notes is "report" in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It now reads at the second line at the bottom of page 5: "This platoon had to report to the commander of the company, and he reported to the commander of the battalion." Is that correct? Then the English version seems to be correct, and it may be a problem in the B/C/S translation. Next one, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Again, at page 6, paragraph 22, second line from the bottom: "The events in which Croatian army personnel participated either as victims or as participants in combat and other events of interest." Instead of "in combat," it should read: "In incidents and other events that were of interest from the security point of view."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the word "incident" now reads "incidents and other events that were of interest from the security point of view." That's on the record. The next one, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. President, if I may be allowed to explain what my corrections are based on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, most important at this moment is that we have the right version. What was wrong in the earlier one is not something that bothers us at this -- greatly. But if that is different, if the parties are interested in that, they will certainly ask you about it. Please with the next one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Page 7, paragraph 24: "Again commanders of battalions of military police are responsible to the military police administration in accordance to the management and professional line." This is how it should read. Or expert and control line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you would say, "based on the expert and control line," rather than the administrative and professional line. Is that correctly understood? That's on the record. Next one, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, the same page, 7, paragraph 25, last line, it reads: "It is submitted to the commander about the task that was taken -- that was carried out, and it should read: "To the commander too ..."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: To the commander as well, t-o-o.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we would then have to read that they would go back to the commander as well, and not the commander who had issued the task.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's on the record. Next one, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me. If we could return to the previous correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I was just looking at the transcript; I thought I heard it that way. The transcript read that the witness said based on the management and professional line or the expert and control line. I wasn't -- I just wonder if there could be some -- whether he was indicating that either of those of terms would be used because it may be used later on as well so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We can check that. I understood your previous question, second line of paragraph 24, that where you said the "management and professional line;" whereas in English, at this moment, it reads "administrative and professional line" that that should be replaced by "expert and control line." But if that is not the case, please tell us what exactly you wanted to change.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. Now we're talking about paragraph 24.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... we go back to your previous correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I entered my corrections on the basis of the transcript of my interview, in which I had a status of a suspect. That was taken in May 2004. I took the words that were in the transcript, and I wanted to have them in the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And could you please tell us then exactly what words you would like to use instead of what words, as we find them at this moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want it to read: Expert and control.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Instead of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Administrative and professional.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is how I understood your correction. Mr. Tieger, that sufficiently clarifies the matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we have gone through the last line of paragraph 25, where you said would go back to the commander as well. That's on the record. Then we move on to the next one. That would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, page 7, paragraph 26, five lines from the bottom, where it says: "In order to receive reinforcements from the 57th Military Police Battalion," it's a typo it should read 67th Military Police Battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's how it reads in English. In reads: "Because the commander of the 68th Battalion did not have enough people, he then turned to the administration of the military police for reinforcements from the 67th Battalion of the military police in Zagreb," and that is correct, from what I understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the next one, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 8, paragraph 29, line 3: "Then disciplinary proceedings would be stood, and he would be handed over to the commander of that platoon." Or, rather, "that soldier." It should be -- it should read: "Disciplinary report would be committed, and he would be handed over to his commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so the word "charge" is now replaced by "they would write a disciplinary report and submit it to the soldier's commander." It's on the record. Next one, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, page 8, paragraph 30, line 3 from the bottom: "The next 5 per cent had experience in police because they served their national service in the military police." And it should read: "In the military police of the former JNA."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's how it reads in English. So that's correct. Now, I noted another difference, that is that another 5 per cent had some military police knowledge, but you just spoke about experience. Is knowledge or experience the right expression?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the course of their national service in the Yugoslav people's army, in the course of the 18 months, which was the usual length of the national service, these men were military police officers; it was their specialty. In the first six months they undertook specialist training for the military police, and in the next 12 months they actually worked as military police in the Yugoslav people's army, so you can speak about ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That sounds like experience which includes knowledge gained during that experience and training. That's on the record. Next one, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 8, paragraph 32, line 4 from the bottom: "In other words had we checked the criminal records of all of the military police members that we caught or found in the Ministry of Interior," it should actually read: "Through the criminal records kept by the Ministry of Interior, we were able to run checks on all members of the military police whom we had found in military police units."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you intend to say that -- that they are not necessarily caught but just found in the military police units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the Croatian translation, it is very important, this distinction between catch or find. As I gave my statement, what I meant was that when we went out in the field and when we were trying to see what the situation was in the military police at that time, I came across -- I found people who claimed that they were military police and they had that as -- in their files in the Croatian army; whereas if you say catch, "hvatati" in Croatian, then this is the term that you use when you catch a perpetrator of a crime and when this person is then processed by the police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So it now reads that: "All members of the military police that we found, we checked their criminal records," et cetera. It's on the record. The next one, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 9, paragraph 33, line 3 from the bottom in the Croatian version: "As a police officer I knew what crimes were dirty or more serious and also what crimes were committed because people wanted to profit from them." Instead of this term that "people wanted to profit," it should read that are committed out of base motives or greed. This is it legal terminology that is used in the Croatian Criminal Code, base motives and greed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then 33 reads: "I also knew which ones were the dirty and most serious crimes and those crimes that were committed out of basic motives and greed." That's on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, sorry, the distinction between basic and base.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, base, yes. Base motives and greed. That's now how we understand your statement. Mr. Lausic, the next one, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, at page 9, paragraph 34, line 7: "You can create a good military officer from such a man." It should read: "It is possible to create a good military police officer from such a man."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It now reads: "From these it is possible that you create a good military police officer." Next one, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, page 9, last line in paragraph 34: "If the units wanted to accept him, return to their military units." It should read: "To other units of the Croatian army."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's on the record, "other units of the Croatian army" instead of "their military units." Next one, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 10, paragraph 38: "The first rank that I received was the rank of a brigadier colonel." The word "brigadier" which is there in the Croatian army should be deleted from the Croatian version, because the first rank that I received was one of colonel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. In English it reads: "The first rank that I got was the rank of a colonel, lieutenant-colonel ..." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The English version is correct. Could you take us to the next one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, page 10, paragraph 38, line 4: "Since I had a rank of superintendent in the police," it should read "chief superintendent."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's how it reads in English. So that's correct in the English version. Please proceed, Mr. Lausic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, paragraph 38 at page 10, line 4 from the bottom. "At that time we did not have those ranks brigadni [phoen] general, brigade general, or stozani [phoen] brigadier, which is -- which would be staff brigadier. What should actually be there is the rank of brigadier general or staff general.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, in English it reads: "We didn't have brigadier general," the rank of brigadier general or staff brigadier, and now you say that should be -- should be staff general? I read it again in English and, please, correct me -- if it's right we leave it as it is. Please correct me in detail when it is wrong. It now reads in English: "I must inform you that at the time we didn't have brigadier general, the rank of brigadier general, or staff brigadier." Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the English version stays as it is. Could you take us to the next one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again at page 10, third line in paragraph 39: "The Main Staff of the Croatian army published general rules of the armed forces." Instead of what it says in the Croatian version which is "would publish," it should read just "publish."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In English it reads "issued" which has the same meaning, from what I understand. "Published" is even a bit more, but I would say generals of the armed forces that are issued apparently were published. That's on the record. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, at page 10, paragraph 40, line 4, "perhaps even for those who served as conscripts." The word "perhaps" should be deleted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's on the record. Next one, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, page 10, paragraph 41, line 5: "Every citizen of the Republic of Croatia was duty-bound to report a crime. On the 7th of December 1991, the President of the Republic issued an instruction published in the Official Gazette number 67/91." It should read: "The President of the Republic issued a decree about the organisation, work and scope of the judiciary in a state of war," et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The word "instructions" is replaced by a more precise reference, a decree about the organisation, work, and scope of the judiciary, and that's not the full title, from what I understand. Please proceed, next one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 11, paragraph 42: "A military court applies to everyone. There is no special code for the military or -- and for civilians. It applies to everyone." Instead of the words "there is no special code for the military and for the civilians," it should read: "The Criminal Code applies to everyone, both to civilians and to the members of the Croatian army."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The correction about the applicability of the Criminal Code applying to everyone, whether military or civilian, is on the record. Could you take us to your next one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 11, paragraph 45, line 2: "Once military courts and military prosecutor's offices were set up within the military police, there was a need to set up a special military crime police sector." It should read: "Separate speciality," which would be the criminal military police, instead of the word "sector," it should be speciality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What do you mean exactly there by speciality? A special unit, or is that what you refer to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me be very specific here. The military police had three specialities. It was the basic military police, general duty military police, traffic military police, and criminal military police. And those were the specialities within the military police, as an arm within the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we would say, To set up a special branch of criminal military police, would that ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes, that would perhaps be the closest approximation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The word "area" is replaced by "branch." Next one, Please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, page 11, paragraph 46, line 2: "And Ante Gugic from the Zagreb police became a member of the military police administration." It should read: "Became the chief of the criminal police section or department."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is on the record.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, at page 11, paragraph 46, line 5: "The minister appointed Ante Gugic, the chief of the criminal police odsjek in the military police administration." It should read "odjel department," because odjel is a higher -- in the hierarchy. It can have several odsjek, so he was appointed the chief of the odjel department, not of odsjek or section.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It now reads at this moment in English that the minister had appointed Ante Gugic as a chief of the criminal police department. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in the military police administration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I think that the English text is correct. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again at page 11, the same paragraph, 46. It's line three from the bottom: "Markica Rebic was appointed the assistant defence minister for security." That post did it not exist. This is how it should read: "He was appointed the assistant -- the deputy assistant defence minister for security." At that time, the assistant defence minister was Mr. Josip Perkovic, and Mr. Markica Rebic was appointed his deputy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It reads in English: "Markica Rebic was appointed deputy assistant for the minister for security." And then between brackets: "This post did not previously exist."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the English is correct. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 12, paragraph 50, last line: "There was no cordon sanitaire for the soldiers." It should actually read: "There was no sterilisation zone for soldiers for mines, shells, explosives, and rounds." In this sense the term "sterilisation" is a technical term.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, sterilisation here refers to mines, shells, and explosives and rounds. You would say, it is directly related to ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Primarily of weapons too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's -- this clarification is on the record. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 13, paragraph 56, the third line from the bottom, there is an obvious typographical error: "The military police cannot arrest a member of the Croatian army." Instead of "military police" it should say "civilian police."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see a reference in this paragraph to the civilian police and a few lines further down to the MUP, which seems to refer to the same. I think the English version is correct. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 14, paragraph 57. I'm going to read all of it, all of paragraph 57, because this is not my statement. These are the words of the investigator, Mr. Foster. And it is obvious from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your statement is that he said something.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. All of paragraph 57 does not really show my words. These are Mr. Foster's words, the investigator's words. It is quite obvious if you look at the transcript of the interview I had with him in April 2004.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. In paragraph 57 in English it starts by saying: "You say ..." which mean that the person interviewed, that's you, refer to what the interviewer is telling the interviewed person and apparently serves as introduction that may follow. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know if the witness is saying that was not his words and shouldn't be part of this statement. That's how I was understanding him to be raising his objection to Mr. Foster's statements being included within his witness statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now I see this is a technique which is used in some systems to make clear that someone else says something. But, Mr. Lausic, you say you didn't even put on the record what someone else said. You refrained from saying anything about that. Is that -- did you repeat the words, or is it just that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My answer is contained in paragraph 58.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's then be -- let's try to resolve it. What you read in paragraph 57, is that what the investigator said, what he told you; or is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exactly. Those were the words that he used when he addressed me before he put his specific question. When he said that he had talked to civilian policemen, and he did talk to them, and he said that they had said that they did not have authority over the military, over military personnel. Since this is a witness statement, it is my understanding that paragraph 57 should be part of my very own statement, but that is it not the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it's clear in 57 that what is in there. Other words not of the interviewed person, but you now tell us that the interviewer spoke those words. That's clear and on the record. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 14, paragraph 58, the second line from the top: "The first stage is reporting a certain incident." Instead of "reporting," it should read "registering a certain incident."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's how it reads in English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next one, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 14, also paragraph 58, line 6 from the bottom: "The civilian police can complete criminal processing there, arrest that person, and take that person to the police station," et cetera. It would be right to say "the military police can complete criminal processing there," and so on and so forth. The rest is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just verify whether I understood you correctly. Yes, the -- you say and that -- the criminal military policemen begins with the criminal investigation, and that one can end in two ways to have these criminal proceedings completed there by the military police. He arrests the person. Is that your correction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Mr. President, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please take us to your next correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, page 14, paragraph 61, we have the same situation like with paragraph 57. Since everything contained in paragraph 61 is actually what the investigator stated, Mr. Brian Foster, and that can be established by looking at the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's clear. Now that is not the words you spoke; but reading it now, is that what he said to you? Were these words spoken by the person that interviewed you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So even if you may not have put the words of that other person on the record at that time, you now confirm that this is what he said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I raise -- I'm slightly concerned because the witness statement we're looking at should be the evidence and testimony of this witness. The words of Mr. Foster or whatever he may have said are not to be the words of this witness within this witness statement, and accordingly, the issue should be whether he agrees with what was said or disagrees for it to exist within the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but if he just -- Mr. Kay, if Mr. Lausic now tell us that that is what Mr. Foster said at that time, that I find nothing else then that those apparently were words spoken by -- whether he agrees or not what was said is, at least from this paragraph, does not appear. So it's just a factually establishing what Mr. Foster said during the interview, nothing more, nothing less.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that appears now from the testimony given by Mr. Lausic at this moment and not from paragraph 61, because he says, I did not speak those words. It was Mr. Foster who said it. It is presented as if he more or less repeated the words of Mr. Foster. That is not confirmed at this moment that he spoke those words during the interview, repeating the words of Mr. Foster. The only thing we know now is that the testimony, at this moment is, that those were words spoken by Mr. Foster, whether he agrees, disagrees, and whether it is relevant, or whether we could do without, it may shed some light as to how the question was introduced to which we may find answers at a later stage. It's not an answer by this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What I was looking at, Your Honour, whether it should be excised totally from the document because it is not the statement of the witness, which would be, in my view, the appropriate way of having his witness statement before the Court. To have it in this form means that we are introducing something in a different form than this witness's witness statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do see that it is more or less a foreign element in the witness statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time you're asking for quite an exercise with the same result, perhaps not technically, but those words apparently, and that's what we hear from the witness now, apparently were spoken by the -- Mr. Foster, and they are not part of the statement he gave at the time. So whether we take them out and then have it reconstructed on the transcript of today is, of course, a technical matter rather than anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. I notice Your Honours making corrections on Your Honours' statements, as I guess we are all doing as well, in the same way. We've put a line through it as not being his testimony, his evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's -- at least there is no misunderstanding about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let's be slightly clearer on that. In the previous example the witness refers back to what was said, and it is necessary contextually. Sometimes it may [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the technical issue is whether we put on the record that the witness testifies today what was said to him at the time or that we understand the statement in such a way that paragraph 61 does not refer to what the witness repeated as the words of Mr. Foster.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Completely clear, Your Honour, and I think it is it clear on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is just purely an objection for the record in terms of this overall. I have a problem with, just in terms of these statements and in this instances in particular, with the fact that an investigator in the course of an interview of a witness is putting suggestions to the witness about what other people have already said. And I think -- just for the record I think it is it an improper technique then in terms of what the answer -- the answer here may not be problematic but overall to conduct witness interviews with someone and say everyone or many people are saying this, you know, how do you respond to that? Instead of just saying, Could the civilian police take action against soldiers without having to say, Other people have said otherwise?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a way of leading the witness. At the same time to have it on the record at least makes it transparent what was apparently used as an introduction to answers to which he then responded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think the reason that the Defence has a problem with this conceptually is that since it's 92 ter and suppose to be, This is how the witness would testify on direct if the questions were posed to him, this type of question could never be -- not never, but in most often couldn't be posed to him like this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think most important is that we have a complete and correct understanding of what these paragraphs tell us. 57, 61, do not tell us what the witness said, whether or not repeating the words of Mr. Foster, but here Mr. Foster, apparently that's a technique used in some systems, puts into the mouth of the witness what he actually said himself by introducing as, You tell me, or, You say. And that's clear. At the same time the witness now confirms that this is what, actually, Mr. Foster said at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, by way of reference, I've looked at 57. Unlike Mr. Tieger's proposition that it is adopted by the witness, it is it not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, did not say it was adopted. I simply said it was referred to and is contextual. I wasn't saying he adopted or disagreed with it. The text will tell that. So I certainly wasn't trying to reinterpret what was said there, only that it is contextual.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Therefore, it shows there is lack of clarity in my view and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think I explained earlier, quite clearly that as we read it here, it just refers to what Mr. Foster apparently said. We now heard from the witness that he did not use those words during the interview, but he confirms that those words were spoken by Mr. Foster, and I think I said already one page ago that this does not include any confirmation of the correctness or anything. It just reflects what Mr. Foster apparently had said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nothing more, nothing less. Please proceed, Mr. Lausic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. Page 15, paragraph 62, the last line: "The other reason is that the civilian police had had negative experience in clashes with members of the Croatian army, some of whom behaved in an opportunistic manner." It should read as follows: "So the civilian police behaved in an opportunistic manner in some cases."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I formulate it again so as to verify whether I understood you well. "The second reason was that the civilian police had negative experience in conflicts with the members of the Croatian army and so the civilian police behaved in an opportunistic way."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, in fairness to what the witness said, he said in some cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, in some cases. So in some cases, the civilian police based in an opportunistic way.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you take us to the next one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 16, paragraph 65 as continued from the previous page, page 15. The third line from the bottom. "They had military experience." Instead of saying "they had military experience," what should be stated is "they had had some military training," as the transcript correctly states. Experience and training, or education, is quite different in the Croatian language, terminologically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. In English it reads they had a military background which is rather vague. Yes. We change that they had some military training.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next one, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, page 16, paragraph 69, line 1: "In the second subgroup there were professors." The word "professors" should be under quotation marks because the word was used by way of an illustration of their work and the attitude of the officers. I tried to use this word rhetorically when I called them professors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. People with a rather theoretical background. Is that how I have to understand "professors" between brackets or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I shall take the liberty of correcting you. What I meant was the attitude they had towards their soldiers. They treated them as a professor would. They would explain that something that they were doing was not nice or was wrong, but they did not act in a military soldierly fashion issuing strict orders, a softer approach as it were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They were teaching rather than commanding. Is that more or less ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it could be put that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please take us to the next correction. And "professors" is now explained and put between quotation marks.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 18, paragraph 79, line 1. "For example, let us say that there is a case of the crime of poisoning. I did not find the word "poisoning" in the transcript, and I cannot really put it into any context related to my statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. In English it reads: "For example, let's say we have a crime of arson or a crime of murder." That's how it reads in English. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, correct. Arson, yes. Poisoning and arson are not the same thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Arson is right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please take us to the next one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The same page, paragraph 80, line 5 from the top: "From day one, from 1991 onwards, that was the rule." Obviously it was a typo. It should have read "from 1992 onwards."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's put on the record. Next one, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The same page, number 18, paragraph 81, the last line: "As far as I know, we stored all criminal records in the administration of the military police." The word "used" should be on a permanent basis: "We stored them there on a permanent basis."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It reads in English: "As long as I was in the police, the records in the civilian police administration were to be kept for" -- Let me just -- were you referring to the last sentence in the military police? Is it about in the military police administration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "We, as far as I know, we have kept permanently all crime files."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct. That would be the right way to put it. Permanent, Your Honour. "Permanent basis" is missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was a bit confused by the first line where the word "permanently" appears. But your correction is in relation to the last sentence of paragraph 81. The word "permanently" is added. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 19, paragraph 82, line 8 from the top: "And he gave me the fax number with code 048." It should read: "049." It's an obvious typo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's on the record. Next one please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Same page, number 19, the same paragraph, 82, line 11: "And I was told that on the 8th of September 1993 a company of the 71st Battalion in Gospic." Without the word "a" in the sense of one, because there was just this one company, so there is no need to specify that it's one because that was the only one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it now reads: "And I was told that the company of the 71st battalion in Gospic."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct. Thank you, Mr. President. The same page, paragraph 83, line 2: "The battalion of the military police was not stationed only in one position." Instead of the word "one position," what should read should be "one location or locality." Position and locality or location are different terms in Croatian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. "Position" is replaced by "location." Next one, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 20, paragraph 85, line 3: "They would have to send preliminary reports;" whereas, it should read "they should send extraordinary reports," because the two words meaning is completely different in Croatian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it that you're referring -- well, in English, I see that -- and I read it in its context. "For example, attacks even against members of the military police, the use of force, would they have to send an extraordinary report to the military police administration?" Is that ... is that the portion you wanted to correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct. Instead of the word "provisional report" the word "extraordinary" or "interim report" should be used, as stated in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The English text reads "interim report," and now use the word "extraordinary report." I do understand this to be a report not in the regular sequence of reporting, but in between a special report an interim report would have to be sent.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In English] That's true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's understood.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm looking at the clock at this moment. And, Mr. Lausic, the Chamber appreciates very much the precision with which you reviewed your statement. We're now at page 19. We have 52 pages which would take us through the whole morning. Would there be any way -- of course, we could not ask the Prosecution to go through the statement with the witness, but if the parties -- because it seems that most of the changes are rather uncontested. Is there any way of using time in between as well by the two parties with the witness to see whether we can more speedily move on, because otherwise we are -- it takes us the whole day. I'm aware that I'm asking you to sacrifice weekends -- breaks after -- and also I'm asking the witness to sacrifice where there was already complaint about taking the time on the weekends, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I was going to use the break to recover from the forced labour over the weekend, Your Honour, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I was already alluding it that in my -- in my observation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, despite my earlier complaints, my concern is not about either the Prosecution's efforts or -- or even that of the Defence. But I do wonder whether it is fair. That would mean the witness was basically working -- if we work through the break and then we work through the next session, he is working for three and a half hours straight, I think that's a bit much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps I should have relied on the wisdom of my colleagues before I even suggested this. Enjoy your break, Mr. Lausic, and for the parties as well. We'll resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, could I just inquire with the -- the Markac Defence why the Chamber has not yet received the Turkalj, or at least I do understand Mr. Kuzmanovic said the Turkalj translation issues have not been communicated yet. Is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's me, Your Honour. I will get to that forthwith. I had two witnesses last week, so that delayed me, so I will get it as soon as I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Mr. Tieger, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, you were doing just fine in directing the witness to his corrections, so I won't interfere with that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it's not --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm happy to say the same things, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's -- well, if you take over the next session. And perhaps I might intervene now and then to have things on the record. And sometimes, of course, the Chamber's understanding of the corrections made might be of importance. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Lausic, if we could proceed with the corrections to the statement. If you could turn to the next one in order, please.

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. Page 20, paragraphs 86, 87, 88, and 89. I don't have any comments to make in relation to the substance of these paragraphs. What I would like to note, however, is that the statements contained in these paragraphs cannot be found in the transcript of the interview I had with investigators in May 2004. Rather, these are statements that I made which were not taped either on the audio or the videotape back in August 2004 when certain documents were shown to me. In other words, I have no way of comparing the text of the statements contained in paragraphs 86 through 89 with a transcript. I read the paragraphs, I did not observe anything that would not appear to be my statement, but since I don't have the corresponding tapes or transcripts, I cannot compare these statements with my answers given to the questions put to me in August 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Lausic. If you can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC
utterances.text: Page 21, paragraph 91, line 2 from the bottom: "So that only after a conversation with General Krpina ..." It should read instead "Brigadier Krpina" because he had the rank of brigadier and not general.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I apologise to Mr. Tieger. If I could just get a clarification to the witness's penultimate answer. He seems to indicate now that there was -- there are statements in the statement that were not videotaped. I don't know if that's the position of the Office of the Prosecutor as well. Because it is my understanding that this statement is based on what he said in May of 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I will let the witness speak for himself. My understanding of the previous answer was that in August, the witness reviewed the statement, made some additional comments or corrections, and was also shown some documents about which he commented. And one or both of those factors is reflected in the paragraphs he just referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that he -- they were not included in his May statement, and for that reason, there is no audio, because in August no audio was made, and that, therefore, he was unable to compare on an audio basis, what he said in August. But he recognises this as his answers. And he is nodding yes now, so I take that as a confirmation of ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm just -- if that's the case, then there would be just for the purpose of the record in August, then, was he still a suspect under Rule 42, 43, and 44, which would require that these matters be taped?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was my understanding, but please correct me if I'm wrong, that when the witness was interviewed in August that he was not considered to be a suspect anymore; whereas, he was in May. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, based on the -- based on the -- well, he certainly wasn't warned again pursuant to Rule 42 again. That's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The question was, was he a suspect in August of 2004?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Or was he consider a suspect? I haven't inquired, Your Honour, to determine whether or not this procedure was followed because he was no considered a suspect, or because it was a follow-up of the -- of the prior proceedings. If you wish to make that confirmation one way or another, I can. But what is clear is that the witness was not warned under Rule 42.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could get just a clarification for that in the next break, and, then, depending on the answer, outside the presence of the witness, I would just like it put something on the record on this point. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then you were taking the witness back to his previous answer, whereas -- let me just get back to the relevant portion of the transcript. Yes, Mr. Tieger, I was expecting you to say at the moment to say that what the witness said is reflected in the English; last answer he gave, the brigadier.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The last correction you made appears in the accurate way in the English version, Mr. Lausic, so, therefore, that's clear on the record. Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Lausic, if you could continue to the next correction, please.

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC
utterances.text: Page 22, paragraph 97, line 5 from the top: "... then issued weapons and started applying stricter security for commands and commanders." It should in fact read as follows: "First -- firstly the preparation of the operation where they would take charge of certain camps, locations where people who are mobilized would come, where weapons would be issued, and stricter security applied in respect of commands and commanders." Without this correction, the Croatian version of this could be construed to mean that the Croatian army issued them with weapons. What is correct is that the military police provided security for mobilisation assembly points where people were called up would be -- would come and where they would be issued with weapons. So it wasn't the military police that issued them with weapons. Rather, the military police provided security for such places.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's on the record. Now you made -- there's one small difference. You said "stricter security for the commands and the commander," in English, in the singular; whereas, you spoke about "commanders," the plural. Is that -- is it plural or singular?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Commands, i.e., headquarters, where the commander and his staff would be housed, and the commander personally. That's normally how security is organised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Lausic, your next correction, please.

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC
utterances.text: Page 25, paragraph 112, as continued from page 24, the second line from the bottom: "And that all eight of them had previously -- had criminal reports." "Criminal records." What should be said is that: "All eight of them were members of the enemy side and that they were in combat," as was, in fact, correctly stated for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That appears clearly. I think they were members of the enemy of forces, that they were engaged in combat. And these eight persons had criminal reports, as it reads here, submitted against them. You want to change that in "criminal records," or would "criminal reports" be fine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Criminal reports had been filed against them. That would be correct. Because if they were to say that they had criminal records, that would mean that they were already registered somewhere either with the police or courts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it seems that the English text is in every respect correct. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, one matter arises from two previous paragraphs, 107 and 108, which I raise at this stage because it might be appropriate, more appropriate, to deal with it now. In 107 it begins: "You suggest that this particular order from Ademi and 108 you ask ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, similar issue as 57 and 61.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's check that. Mr. Lausic, could you have a look at paragraphs 107 and 108.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's absolutely correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Although halfway paragraph 107 it moves from what apparently the interviewer had told you to your comments on it. Can we then go the first portion, You suggest that, is that what Mr. Foster told you at the time, apart from whether you repeated that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Mr. President. All the words and sentences up until the start of the following sentence: "I can say that this order is not according to military principles in terms of a military vertical structure, but I would not like to draw other's conclusions for this." And save for this sentence, all the other words were uttered by the investigator.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And would that same be true for the whole of paragraph 108; that is, all words spoken by the investigator?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Mr. President. Without looking at the transcript, I could not say -- state that with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it your recollection that the interviewer said words of this kind, as you find them in paragraph 108?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will be very careful and allow for the possibility that one part of the paragraph constitutes a question and the other my answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In 108 I see no answer. I see that in 107 what appears to a question, and then the last two sentences to be your answer. However, in 108, I only see a reference to the words apparently spoken by Mr. Foster, when then paragraph 109 starts saying, "My response is ..." which suggests that 108 reflects the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, but I cannot be certain. In the Croatian language, it starts as follows: "You ask if the commander of the military police should report the commander of his battalion of something that was done, and to say that an order was given to him to do something that he should not." In fact, this entire portion would be me asking the investigator if I understood his question correctly. Because in paragraph 109, I carry on by saying, "My answer, my response is that in any case ..." So paragraph 108 would be me asking the investigator if my understanding of his question was correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, whether we should understand it in that way is another matter. But what I'd like it know is, do you recognise in the text of paragraph 108 the question as it was put to you at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then that resolves the matter. Then let me just take you back where we were. Without soliciting to it, I get the transcript of another case on my screen as well, and I'll just ignore that. But I have to get back to the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lausic, we have dealt with your correction you made at the end of paragraph 112. Could you please move to your next correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Page 25, paragraph 114, line 4 from the bottom. Again it reads that: "Major Ante Gugic was the chief of section," et cetera. The correction would be "chief of the department of the criminal investigation police."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's how it reads in English, "the criminal department within the military police administration." Could you move to the next one, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 26, paragraph 116, same as above, line 3 from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My apologies. Yes, I'm sorry, I had to deal with some technical matters on my screen, where ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 26, paragraph 117, same as above. "The then chief of the criminal investigation section," which should, in fact, read "the criminal investigation department."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We've seen that we find that 116, reflected in a correct way. In 117, it also reads in English, "department." I give Mr. Tieger the lead again. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lausic. If you could direct your attention to the next correction you wish to make.

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC
utterances.text: Page 27, paragraph 120, line 10 from the top: "All the entry/exit wounds were inflicted from the same distance." The correction version should be: "All the entry/exit wounds were inflicted from a distance."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is essentially what the English now says, but I suppose the witness's correction offers a tiny bit of additional clarity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I do understand that entry/exit wounds inflicted from a distance does not mean that they were all inflicted from the same distance. That is, it could be 100 metres, 120 metres, 80 metres which is not the same distance but all from a distance rather compared to nearby. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour, except the English as I -- if I'm directing my attention to the proper portion, it didn't read the same distance; it said from "some distance."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "Some distance," yes, you're right. I misread "some" and "same."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Nevertheless --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's clear now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lausic. Next correction, please.

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC
utterances.text: The same page and the same paragraph, 120, one line further down: "Only one corpse had a entry/exit wound inflicted from a very close or contact range." The term that I used was from absolute range, point-blank range in other words, which means that the barrel rested against the tissue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the option that it could have been from a couple of centimetres is excluded. You say it was contact range, that is, contact between the weapon and the body.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The word "close" is taken out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The correction is noted, and if you could turn to the next correction, please.

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Page 23, paragraph -- page 32, paragraph 151: "Susak went on to say that a meeting was held with the BiH army and the Croatian Defence counsel and that they were heading towards Donji Vakuf and Kulen-Vakuf." The correct version should read: "And that they were moving towards Donji Vakuf" -- "they are moving towards Donji Vakuf and Kulen-Vakuf." In other words present tense, not past tense.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So "are" for "were" in that sentence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least I do not know whether they were would mean necessarily a different thing, but if we make it "are," then it certainly avoids whatever confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Lausic, next correction, please.

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC
utterances.text: The same page, 33, paragraph 151, this sentence continues as follows: "The military police has to act more energetically and prevent all offences." Correction: "The military police should be more energetic in its action or activity."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not certain whether this is reflected in the English. I will read you to what the English text says. It reads: "The military police must be more vigorous in handling and preventing all offences." I see you're nodding yes, which I understand to be a confirmation of the correctness of the -- the accuracy of the English text. Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Lausic, you were about to continue with --

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC
utterances.text: Again page 33, again paragraph 151, Minister Susak's statement continues. That is line 5 from the bottom. And in the sentence: "We have to prevent the possibility that heros of the homeland war be put before a court with his gestures and grimaces, and so on and so forth." It should read as follows: "We must prevent the heros from the homeland war from being put before a court." Mr. President, if you allow me, without this correction, without this terminological correction, this sentence of Mr. Susak's could be interpreted in the following way, it could be understood in the following way: That commanders could prevent the possibility of bringing heros before a court of law; that is to say, something that his sentence did not mean. The point was of his sentence that commanders should realize that some things should not be done so that heros of the homeland war as perpetrators would not be brought before a court. So that's why I repeat what the correction version would be, and that's in line with the transcript: "We must prevent the heros of the homeland war from being brought before a court."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you for that correction, Mr. Lausic. If could you move on in your next correction, please.

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC
utterances.text: Again, page 33, paragraph 151.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the parties check very careful this last portion because it appears on the transcript whether it's transcribed correctly. Because the correction the witness made does not deprive the text as he then read it out from all of its ambiguity. Because whether we're talking about possibility or just about preventing someone to come before a court, there still appears to be a possible interpretation that preventing someone to appear before a court could mean, Don't do anything that could bring you before a court, or let's do everything to ensure that you will not be brought before a court, whatever you have done. So, therefore, I'd like to invite the parties to carefully check the original text in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the two previous sentences, in my view, put in context what the witness is saying if you read those because they were quite clearly instructions that the military police must be more vigorous in handling and preventing offences, commanders must pass on a ban on excessive behaviour and crimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see the context. I'm not blind for that. But, at the same time, the witness refers to the language that appears on the transcript in this specific line, and I would like to have that verified so that there is no doubt about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm sure if you're asking him to verify what he said in May 2004 or verify what is in his notebook from the 2nd of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I think he -- You referred to your transcript of the interview. Is that -- have I understood that correctly? Then I'd like to -- one doesn't exclude the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Actually, that's -- the sentence appears in the -- as an entry in the notebook or in the diary of the 2nd of August. General Lausic, I believe, was then attempting to explain what that sentence means in his suspect interview, and so if there is any ambiguity about the sentence in the 2nd of August diary, it should be put to him now. Because I think that's exactly the point. He was trying to remove any ambiguity about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At this moment he asked for a correction to be made on the basis of the transcript of his interview. At this stage. We are there and not any further. First of all, we should know exactly what his statement reflects, transcript, the notebook, and then, of course, later on we go to the substance of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, just rather than -- in the interests, actually, of economy, Judge, it is not only as I understand the Rule 92 ter process that he is asked, Is this what you said, but would you say this again if these questions were posed to you on direct examination. So there is two prongs here, and if there is anything unclear about -- even if he said something in the May 2004 transcript that is in any way ambiguous, it should be put to him now if he wishes.
